name: Liquid Motion (Motion Design and Cinematography, supplemental, user-requested direction).
visualIdentity: Explicit: droplets or viscous forms stretch, string, merge, split, and elastically settle. The surface may be 2D or 3D, and highlights must not obscure contours. A drop lands, spreads, and gathers into a wordmark, then holds accurate lettering. Glass, iridescence, and validated fluid physics are not required.
suitableUses: Explicit: logo formations and abstract transitions. Inferred from listed pairings: brand stings, beverage or cosmetics titles, and event openers. Music visualizers fit only when a licensed track is supplied. Suitability for text-heavy or physically realistic splash scenes is not established.
limitations: Metaballs cannot hold accurate lettering, so real text must be composited after formation and then remain rigid. The surfaces are not physically accurate. Physical splashes and collisions need a separate simulation baked in Blender. Long kinetic type sequences dilute the fluid hero, and pulsing on every beat reads as jitter.
palette: Example tokens only, and reference-dependent: background #171E2B, foreground #F5ECE0, accent_1 #758FC0, accent_2 #C889A6. Task, brand, or reference colors override these. Gradients are disabled. Checked two-color pairs: foreground on background 14.285:1, background on accent_1 5.128:1, background on accent_2 6.034:1. These checks do not cover composited frames.
motionAndInteraction: Explicit: stretch, merge, split, and elastic settling are driven from composition time, with one owner per animated property. The drop-impact-growth (motion-003) and bounded orb deformation (motion-014) references are optional and apply only if the topic and assets support them. Input interaction for this style is unspecified; a reduced-motion static state is suggested for HTML outputs.
audio: Unspecified for this style; no soundtrack, voice, or effects are required. Beat-mapped merges and splits are suggested only with a supplied track, triggering on major beats. Sound-reactive work needs verified, precomputed audio analysis. Task audio requirements take priority, and speech must stay intelligible and synchronized with picture.
assetRequirements: Real font files for the wordmark or phrase must be loaded before rendering. Lettering is composited rather than approximated by metaballs, though verified glyph distance fields are an option. Physical splash work needs baked simulation caches. No reference artwork, exact copy, or audio assets are specified; supplied assets and exact colors override the example palette.
combinations: Suggested: style-093 for real-font kinetic type that takes over once the drop gathers, keeping fluid highlights off letter contours. Style-105 for beat-mapped merges and splits, but only with a supplied track. Motion-003 or motion-014 may pair if compatible. Alternatives include SVG morphing with GSAP MorphSVGPlugin, a Blender bake scripted with bpy, or Remotion.
productionApproach: Style renderer: WebGL with GLSL or Three.js for SDF metaballs, using fullscreen shading in 2D or ray marching in 3D; p5.js or Paper.js are optional. Motion engine: GLSL driven by composition time. HyperFrames is primary, and Remotion is used only if HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation exists, with the reason recorded. Validate with check, snapshot, and render, then verify direct, backward, and out-of-order seeks plus decoded frames.
